title: Static Global Robot Localization in 2D Occupancy Maps using an Evolutionary Algorithm
description:
Global localization of a static robot in a known 2D occupancy map, formulated as an optimization problem: a population of candidate poses (x, y, theta) evolves so that the range scan simulated from each candidate matches a single observed scan.

Because the approach returns a population rather than a single estimate, it makes ambiguous environments — where distinct poses produce near-identical scans — directly analysable. The experiment suite measures this across five maps, covering perception ablation, beam-count sensitivity, parameter tuning and a symmetry/scan-equivalence analysis.

The repository contains the full implementation, the five maps, the complete experimental outputs (raw and summarised CSV logs, plots and animations) and the accompanying report.
